n: Sound the alarm! An enemy swoops like an eagle (or vulture) over the Lord’s land, because Israel has broken His covenant and law. Assyria is coming.

f.w: Set the trumpet to thy mouth

f.g: Or vulture—a bird of prey descending.
Here the land or people of Israel, God’s household.

n: In trouble, Israel cries, “My God, we know You!” But their claim is empty; their lives show they don’t.
Israel has thrown away what is good, so enemies will chase them.
They made kings without consulting God and made idols with their silver and gold—to their own destruction. Israel’s last kings came to power by assassination, not God’s choosing.

f.w: They have set up kings, but not by me

n: God rejects Samaria’s calf idol. “How long will they be incapable of innocence?” Jeroboam I had set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.
A craftsman made it, so it can’t be God. The calf of Samaria will be smashed to pieces. Idols are only as powerful as their makers.

f.w: the workman made it; therefore it is not God

n: A famous proverb: they sow the wind and will reap the whirlwind. Their foolish choices will produce a harvest of destruction far greater than what they planted. Even what grows will be eaten by foreigners.

f.w: they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind

n: Israel is swallowed up and becomes, among the nations, like a useless pot that no one wants.

f.w: a vessel wherein is no pleasure

n: They went to Assyria like a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim pays for allies like hiring lovers—an especially shameful picture.

f.w: a wild ass alone by himself
f.g: A stubborn, wandering donkey; a pun on Ephraim (pere’ = wild donkey).

n: Though they bargain with the nations, God will gather them for judgment, and they will begin to suffer under the burden imposed by the “king of princes”—the Assyrian emperor’s heavy tribute.

f.g: The Assyrian emperor, who called himself king of kings.

n: Ephraim built many altars to deal with sin—but they became places for sinning. Religion without obedience multiplies guilt.
God wrote out His law for them in great detail, yet they treated it as foreign—something irrelevant to them.

f.w: I have written to him the great things of my law

n: They offer sacrifices and eat the meat, but the Lord doesn’t accept them. He will remember their sins and send them back to “Egypt”—into bondage again.

f.g: A symbol of renewed slavery and exile.

n: Israel forgot its Maker and built palaces; Judah built fortified cities. God will send fire on them. Trusting in buildings and defenses instead of God is futile.

f.w: I will send a fire upon his cities
